chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Aban, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-'Attar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "I have debt, and dirhams come into my possession; if I distribute them among them, nothing significant will fall to them."
"Should I perform hajj with it, or distribute it among the creditors?" He عليه السلام said: "Perform hajj with it, and pray to Allah to settle your debt for you, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills."

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمُ: silver coins or monetary funds in hand
key_terms.الدَّيْنُ: debt owed by a person to others
key_terms.الْغُرَمَاءِ: creditors to whom the debt is owed
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: to settle or discharge, here referring to paying off debt

ai.seo_question: If a debtor has only a small amount of money, should he use it for hajj or divide it among his creditors?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a debtor who receives a small amount of money insufficient to meaningfully satisfy his creditors. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام instructs him to perform hajj with it and to make du'a to Allah to settle his debt. The report relates to fiqh concerning debt, hajj, and reliance upon Allah alongside worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2906 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Aban, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-‘Attar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "I have debt, and some dirhams come into my possession. If I divide them among my creditors, they will not settle anything significant. Should I use them for Hajj, or should I distribute them among the creditors?"
Imam (as) said: "Perform Hajj with them, and pray to Allah (swt) to help you settle your debt, God willing."
